import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 1

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
-/

namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture1

open SimpleGraph

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 1](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph `G` the maximum number of leaves of a spanning
tree satisfies `Ls(G) ≥ n(G) + 1 - 2·m(G)` where `n(G)` counts vertices and
`m(G)` is the size of a maximum matching.

A formal proof reduces to a spanning tree `T`. If `I` is the set of non-leaves
of `T`, Hall's theorem applied to a bipartition of `T` gives a matching `M`
with `|I| + 1 ≤ 2 * |M|`. Since `|V|` is the sum of the numbers of leaves and
non-leaves, and every matching and leaf count constructed in `T` is admissible
for the corresponding supremum in `G`, the stated inequality follows.
-/

@[category research solved, AMS 5,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/MiskinAleksandr23/WOWII-1/blob/eda16f6e96b313bd112351ae9859133b77d537c9/WOWII1/GraphConjecture1.lean"]
theorem conjecture1 {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]
    (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (h_conn : G.Connected) :
    (Fintype.card α : ℝ) + 1 - 2 * matchingNumber G ≤ (Ls G : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture1

reformulations.difference: The source's finite combinatorial maxima are represented by suprema of real-valued cardinalities, and the inequality is expressed in ℝ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A finite graph has finitely many subgraphs. The matching family contains the empty matching, and connectedness guarantees a spanning tree. Consequently both supremum sets are finite and nonempty, so their suprema are attained maxima. Matching sizes count unordered edges, and leaf counts count degree-one vertices of the spanning tree. In scratch.lean, Review.bound_iff_concrete proves the displayed inequality equivalent to existence of a maximum matching M and spanning tree T satisfying the natural-number inequality n + 1 ≤ 2|M| + leaves(T).

sources_consulted: E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjecture 1 and its 1996/December 2004 remarks, archived at http://web.archive.org/web/20260723161800id_/http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html

Local repository at c90271f0fa9b9533883fca1478ab9ac0de036522: FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Matching.lean and SpanningTree.lean; WrittenOnTheWallII/README.md and relevant matching tests in Test.lean.

Installed Mathlib sources: Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Matching.lean, Subgraph.lean, Acyclic.lean, Finite.lean, Connectivity/Connected.lean; real-supremum definitions and finite-supremum lemmas in Algebra/Order/Archimedean/Real/Basic.lean and Order/ConditionallyCompleteLattice/Finset.lean.
review.notes: The sole theorem faithfully states Conjecture 1. The source remarks explicitly restrict the bound to connected graphs on at least two vertices and credit Fajtlowicz's 1996 proof, supporting both [Nontrivial α] and research solved. The live source was unavailable; the archived source supplied the statement and remarks. Boundary checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean establish zero invariants for empty and singleton edgeless graphs, failure of the bound for the excluded singleton, and matchingNumber K₂ = 1 and Ls K₂ = 2. The linked proof and its dependency were kernel-checked in /workspace/review/externalProofCheck.lean after mechanical Mathlib API adaptations; #print axioms reports only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.
